info.name: Cinema-booking Collection
info.description:
# Cinema Booking API — Postman Workspace Documentation

Welcome to the official Postman collection for the **Cinema Booking API**. This documentation serves as a blueprint and comprehensive testing suite for a modern movie ticketing and cinema management platform.

---

## 🔐 Authentication, Environment & Automation

The API utilizes secure **JWT (JSON Web Token)** authentication, heavily optimized within this collection for rapid, automated testing.

### 🌐 Environment & Variables

To execute these requests, ensure that your Postman environment is actively set to **`Local Dev`**. It manages the following global states:

- `{{baseUrl}}` — Defaults to `http://localhost:7000` for localized development.
    
- `{{userPassword}}` — A unified, pre-configured testing password applied across all mock profiles to streamline the authentication lifecycle without hardcoding credentials into individual requests.
    
- `{{jwt_token}}` — Dynamically updated after any login sequence.
    

### ⚙️ Token Management Workflow

1. **Targeted Testing Accounts:** Inside the `auth` folder, separate folders for **Post registers requests** and **Post logins requests** contain dedicated, identity-specific requests for standard testing personas (e.g., `lcroft`, `kmitnick`, `mscott`, `nwilliams`, `asmith`).
    
2. **Token Extraction:** Upon executing any successful request from the login folder, the server returns a JSON payload containing the `accessToken`.
    
3. **Automated Environment Storage:** A pre-configured Postman test script automatically extracts this token and saves it directly to your **`Local Dev`** **environment file** as the `jwt_token` variable.
    
4. **Inheritance:** All protected endpoints across the workspace inherit this token seamlessly via **Bearer Authentication**.
    

---

## 🗂️ Collection Architecture & Request Routing

Every entity within this collection follows a standardized, highly predictable folder taxonomy separated by HTTP methods: `GET requests`, `POST requests`, `PATCH requests`, and `DELETE requests`.

### 📌 Universal CRUD Behavior (GET & DELETE Profiles)

For all resources below (**Movies**, **Sessions**, **Bookings**, **Halls**, **Seats**), the query and removal structures remain identical:

- **Fetch All / List:** A base route execution (e.g., `GET {{baseUrl}}/movies`) instantly retrieves the complete array of records.
    
- **Fetch Single Entity:** Appending an ID directly to the path (e.g., `GET {{baseUrl}}/movies/1`) isolates and returns that specific record.
    
- **Purge Records:** Executing the matching `DELETE` endpoint with an explicit entity ID permanently removes it from the host database.
    

---

## 📁 Detailed Resource & PATCH Specifications

### 🎬 Movies

Handles full administrative control over the cinema's film catalog.

- **POST:** Spawns a new movie card complete with core metadata.
    
- **PATCH Modifications:** Tailored explicitly to alter critical operational properties. Updates the film's **`ageRating`** (age restrictions) and **`duration`** fields.
    

### 📅 Sessions

Controls the real-time timeline matrix and showtimes for screenings.

- **POST:** Schedules a distinct screening by linking a movie entry to a specific time.
    
- **PATCH Modifications:** Dynamically updates live operational parameters. Specifically alters the current session **`status`** and**`basePrice`**.
    

### 🎟️ Bookings

Manages user ticketing transactions and reservation flows.

- **POST:** Reserves an available seat for an individual customer.
    
- **PATCH Modifications:** Allows for operational booking overrides and ticket re-assignments. Updates the specific **`hallId`** (assigned theater room) and **`seatId`** (physical location/seat coordinates).
    

### 🏛️ Halls

Configures the physical viewing rooms and layout properties of the cinema (e.g., VIP, IMAX, Green).

- **POST:** Creates and registers a new theater room layout.
    
- **PATCH Modifications:** Targets identification adjustments. Specifically rewrites the registered **`name`** of the hall.
    

### 💺 Seats

Configures individual structural nodes and seating availability charts within the theaters.

- **POST:** Maps new seats into a specific hall matrix.
    
- **PATCH Modifications:** Adjusts tier classifications. Specifically toggles the seat type tier between **`vip`** and **`standard`**.

Handles the seat reservation workflow. Allows users to create, view, update, and cancel bookings for a specific session. Each booking links a user to one or more seats in a session.

item.description: **Delete halls requests** — Requests for permanently removing a hall by its ID.

Manages the physical screening halls within the cinema. Each hall has a name and a seating configuration. Supports listing all halls, retrieving a hall by ID, creating new halls (e.g. VIP, IMAX Laser, Dolby Atmos, 4DX), updating hall details, and deleting halls.

Get seats requests
item.description: **Get seats requests** — Requests for retrieving seats within a hall. Includes listing all seats for a given hall and fetching a specific seat by its ID.

item.name: Post seats requests
item.description: **Post seats requests** — Requests for adding new seats to a hall. Accepts seat type (standard or VIP) and associates the seat with the specified hall.

item.name: Patch seats requests
item.description: **Patch seats requests** — Requests for updating the type of an existing seat (e.g. changing from standard to VIP).

item.name: Delete seats requests
item.description: **Delete seats requests** — Requests for permanently removing a seat from a hall by its ID.

Manages individual seats within a hall. Each seat belongs to a hall and has a type (standard or VIP). Supports listing all seats in a hall, retrieving a specific seat, adding new seats, updating seat types, and deleting seats.

item.name: auth
Post registers requests
item.description: **Post registers requests** — Requests for creating a new user account. Sends user credentials (e.g. email and password) to the registration endpoint and returns the newly created user record.

item.name: Post logins requests
item.description: **Post logins requests** — Requests for authenticating an existing user. Submits credentials to the login endpoint and returns a JWT token on success, which is stored for use across the collection.

Handles user identity and access. Contains requests for registering a new user account and logging in with existing credentials. A successful login returns a JWT token that is stored in the `jwt_token` collection variable and automatically applied to all subsequent requests that require authentication.
